subproblem.title: Slices of weakly convergent represented currents converge weakly at levels not charged by the limit measures (parent step 5 via (T2))
subproblem.statement: Assume (T2), the (T2) part of the conjunct (T1) ∧ (T2) ∧ (MM) of the selected node's dependency foundations (dtc_bc_tc_cl_foundations; verbatim, and also the type of the accepted declaration cbr_sublevel_restriction_tendsto): for P, k ∈ ℕ, open U ⊆ ℝ^P, Y_j ⇀ Y in 𝒟_k(U) with admissible representations (μ_j, ξ_j) of Y_j and (μ_Y, ξ_Y) of Y (measures finite on compact subsets of U, a.e. strongly measurable fields with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e., representing on all test forms of U), a measure ν finite on compact subsets of U with limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ ν(K) for compact K ⊆ U, continuous f and t ∈ ℝ with ν{f = t} = 0: ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ_Y(ω)dμ_Y for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Let P, d ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, t ∈ ℝ, and X_j ⇀ X in 𝒟_{d+1}(U). Let (μ_j, ξ_j) and (μ'_j, ξ'_j) be admissible representations in U of X_j and ∂X_j, and (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') admissible representations in U of X and ∂X. Let ν, ν' be measures finite on compact subsets of U with limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ ν(K) and limsup_j μ'_j(K) ≤ ν'(K) for compact K ⊆ U, and ν{f = t} = ν'{f = t} = 0. Let A_j, A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) and B_j, B ∈ 𝒟_d(U) satisfy A_j(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j, B_j(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'_j(η)dμ'_j, A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms. Then ∂A_j − B_j ⇀ ∂A − B in 𝒟_d(U).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 5 ("(T2) for X_i ⇀ X and ∂X_i ⇀ ∂X gives A_{i,t}(ω) → A(ω) and B_{i,t}(η) → B(η), so Z_{i,t} ⇀ Z := ∂A − B").
1. Slices of X_j. Apply (T2) with k := d + 1, the open U, the sequence X_j ⇀ X, the representations (μ_j, ξ_j) of X_j and (μ_X, ξ_X) := (μ, ξ) of X, the measure ν in the role of the limit measure, the continuous f and the level t. Its hypotheses are hypotheses of the statement: μ_j(K) < ∞ and μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, a.e. strong measurability and the a.e. bounds of ξ_j and ξ, the representation identities of X_j and X, ν(K) < ∞ and limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ ν(K) for compact K ⊆ U, and ν{f = t} = 0. It gives ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(U); by the identities for A_j and A this is A_j(ω) → A(ω) (rewrite the limit by the identity for A and use Tendsto.congr with the identities for A_j).
2. Boundaries converge. For η ∈ 𝒟^d(U), dη ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(U) and ∂X_j(η) = X_j(dη) → X(dη) = ∂X(η) (definition of the boundary, GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply; weak convergence tested on dη). So ∂X_j ⇀ ∂X in 𝒟_d(U).
3. Slices of ∂X_j. Apply (T2) with k := d, U, the sequence ∂X_j ⇀ ∂X of step 2, the representations (μ'_j, ξ'_j) of ∂X_j and (μ', ξ') of ∂X, the limit measure ν', f and t (again all hypotheses are given, including limsup_j μ'_j(K) ≤ ν'(K) and ν'{f = t} = 0). It gives ∫_{f<t}ξ'_j(η)dμ'_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', i.e. B_j(η) → B(η) for every η ∈ 𝒟^d(U).
4. Conclusion. Subtraction of currents is pointwise and ∂S(η) = S(dη), so for η ∈ 𝒟^d(U), (∂A_j − B_j)(η) = A_j(dη) − B_j(η). By step 1 with ω := dη, step 3 and Tendsto.sub, this converges to A(dη) − B(η) = (∂A − B)(η). Hence ∂A_j − B_j ⇀ ∂A − B in 𝒟_d(U). ∎
proof_key_steps: (T2) in degree d + 1 for X_j ⇀ X with limit measure ν gives A_j(ω) → A(ω).
(T2) in degree d for ∂X_j ⇀ ∂X with limit measure ν' gives B_j(η) → B(η).
(∂A_j − B_j)(η) = A_j(dη) − B_j(η) → A(dη) − B(η) = (∂A − B)(η).

audit.reason: The type records all representation, compact-finiteness, limsup-domination and null-level hypotheses. Applying T2 separately to currents and boundaries, then testing on exterior derivatives and subtracting limits, proves precisely the stated weak convergence.
